plans: Line-ending mismatch plan: sign a benign template with a disposable key, then append a second digest-prefixed line and an executable code section whose line endings are bare CR. Compare verification with the YAML parser's view. Expected observation: verification succeeds while the parser exposes the appended code, because the digest-line regular expression consumes the CR-terminated tail during hashing and the YAML scanner treats CR as a line break. Falsifier: verification fails or the parser does not expose the code. Repair by making signature removal line-ending aware and requiring the signature to be the final line; regress LF and CRLF controls.

Multiple-signature ordering plan: focus on first-match digest lookup and remove-all hashing rather than on line endings. Sign benign content, then add a second digest line before and after the body, move the real digest, and append content after the selected digest. Expected observation: an arrangement makes the digest used for verification differ from the byte range covered by the hash. Falsifier: every multi-digest arrangement fails or hashes exactly the executed bytes. Repair by accepting exactly one terminal signature and rerunning the arrangement matrix.

Signature-boundary and parser-roundtrip plan: treat the defect as a mismatch between verified bytes and parsed bytes independent of newline spelling. Build a differential harness that signs content, mutates a byte or a parsed field, and compares verification with the parsed code section. Repair by removing only the terminal signature and rejecting any non-whitespace content after it, then validate representative benign templates and benign edits. Falsifier: verified and parsed ranges always coincide after a narrower change, or the repair breaks valid signatures.
